blocks.text: A linguistic category of words sharing syntactic or morphological behaviour and semantic properties, such as noun or verb.
A word that functions as the name of a specific object or set of objects, such as person, animal, place, word, thing, phenomenon, substance, quality, or idea.
A word that modifies a noun or noun phrase or describes a noun’s referent.
A word that indicates an action, event, or state of being.
A word that modifies a verb, adjective, other adverbs, or various other types of words, phrases, or clauses.
A word or a group of words that one may substitute for a noun or noun phrase.
A number word, a simple or compound word for a number often having particular grammatical attributes depending on the language.
Any of a class of non-inflecting words and multiword terms typically employed to connect a following noun or a pronoun, in an adjectival or adverbial sense, with some other word.
A word used to join other words, phrases, or clauses together into sentences.
A part of speech that has no inherent lexical definition but must be associated with another word to impart meaning, often a grammatical category.
A phrase or word with no particular grammatical relation to a sentence but which serves to express emotion or as a filled pause.
A form of a verb that may function as an adjective, noun or adverb.
A participle that modifies a verb in the same sentence and is equivalent to an adverbial clause in English.
Exercises: which term each definition is of. Review Terms, at the foot of the page, drills this module's terms.
